title: The doctor's memory search probe splits text differently from the FTS5 tokenizer for combining marks and private-use characters
outcome: Memory search builds its query terms the way the unicode61 tokenizer split the indexed text, so a correctly indexed memory holding combining marks or private-use characters is found by its own words, and doctor keeps passing it.
acceptance: Doctor regression guard: a correctly indexed project memory whose text holds a standalone combining mark (U+0345, U+05B0 or U+093E), a decomposed accent inside a word (a U+0301 b), a private-use character inside a word (a U+E000 b), or a mark after a letter (U+0915 U+093E) passes doctor, and removing that memory's genuine object_fts row is still reported as damage; a test covers each case.

A memory search for a correctly indexed memory's own words holding each of those characters finds the memory: the standalone marks U+0345, U+05B0 and U+093E between words, a U+0301 b, and a U+E000 b; the test fails before the fix (the letter-or-digit split misses all five) and passes after it, and the mark after a letter keeps being found.

completion.summary: Memory search now splits its query where SQLite's unicode61 tokenizer split the indexed text: it classifies non-ASCII characters in a private in-memory FTS5 table per query. Words with a decomposed accent or a private-use character are searched whole, and lone marks are dropped. So a correctly indexed memory is found by its own words. Doctor keeps passing such memories and still reports a removed index row. The persisted index is unchanged, so no repair is needed. Landed as 6441d43.
